header.description: Partial page index of St. Petersburg, National Library of Russia, Evr. II B 55, over the National Library of Israel's images of the codex, whose record calls it Ms. EVR II B 247, 55 and has two parts. It grows page by page, and each record's de_note says who read it, when and at what resolution. A record identifies a page by de_nli_part, by de_nli_image, the image's number in its downloaded filename, and by de_fl_id, the NLI file id in the same filename; de_shelfmark follows the part, Part B's images being taken as B 55's. de_first_atom_* names the first atom the page held and de_last_atom_* its last atom. An atom whose _state is lost was not seen: de_first_atom_basis says how it was inferred, and de_first_surviving_atom_* names the first atom that survives; damaged means partly legible. A _ref names a verse by MAM-simple's book id, chapter and verse, as the verse labels of the Aleppo and Cambridge 1753 line-break files do. A _num counts that verse's atoms from 1 in MAM's word sequence in MAM-simple/xml-vtrad-mam/, segmented as the flat streams behind those line-break files segment it: py/py_ac_loc/mam_xml_verses.py's get_verse_words, then a split after every maqaf. So the paseq glyph and a sof pasuq go with the atom before them, and a ketiv/qere contributes its ketiv. Every de_*_text is MAM's LETTERS, UNPOINTED, one space between atoms, lifted from MAM-simple by a script and never typed, and deliberately so: a record locates text on a page, so pointing it would suggest the pointing had been transcribed off the image as well as the letters, which it has not been. Nothing here records what the manuscript has in pointing, accents or meteg. de_text_at_line gives a located verse's atoms on one line and de_text_at_line_ref that line: a page's lines are its 19 ruled lines of main text, counted from the top with blank ones included. de_pencil_numbers lists the pencilled numbers seen at the foot or in the lower-left margin; an empty list means none was seen there.

consumer_notice.summary: This file is a locator index, not a manuscript transcription or a Bible edition.
critical_rules: Text ranges and text cues locate content on photographed pages; they must not be cited as a diplomatic transcription of the manuscript.
Gaps and mid-verse boundaries are meaningful locator evidence; do not round them to whole verses or fill them from another edition.
Line-break and page-geometry annotations are separate supporting data; do not infer either from this entry index.
